scope: REQ-022/023/024 revision 1, AC-1 and AC-2 each, executed under VER-022/023/024 revision 1. Bounded local SQLite headless interface acceptance only.

candidate.qualification: Working-tree candidate, not a claim that HEAD includes the new test/report. Pre-existing uncommitted Verification UI/documentation/register work remains separate. No runtime source changed in this audit.

sourceTree.algorithm: SHA-256 of sorted UTF-8 lines: file SHA-256, two spaces, repository-relative src path, LF. Every file under src is included; exact manifest retained at output/headless-acceptance/source-tree.sha256.

criteria.actual: Performed writes through public core, separate CLI processes outside the checkout, and real headless HTTP/client in requirement/title-string and experiment/score-number projects. Each project contains only its three intended records. Paged query and deterministic export responses agree across interfaces without frontend assets in the disposable working directory.

All three interfaces reject stale schema, object and project guards and missing configured required fields. Structured object conflict details agree; complete recorded exports remain unchanged after rejections. Distinct explicit SQLite paths and HTTP project selections retain independent schemas/populations.

criteria.actual: Dropped the HTTP response only after consuming a committed result; client reports outcome_unknown and sends exactly one POST. Closed the host and repositories, reopened SQLite, then deleted the output and advanced schema. Repeated core/CLI/HTTP lookups and exact explicit replays return the immutable original result without changing the full recorded export. The other project has no matching outcome.

Changed operations and schema/head guards reject with commandId conflict across all interfaces. Changed trusted actor/reason reject at the shared application boundary. Original outcome/export remain unchanged. Rejected new identities remain absent and can be deliberately corrected and committed. Existing outcome tests additionally exercise competing connections and intent isolation.

criteria.actual: Configured missing feature, missing operation, insufficient limit, wrong API identity and old/new contract versions block writes before and after discovery failure. Real discovery is fetched through the headless host; incompatible identity/version responses are deliberately fault-injected. Request logs contain only one GET /api/capabilities, no session or POST; full project export remains unchanged.

Held an actual older successful discovery response while a later check fails on invalid local requirements, malformed response or cancellation. Pending/failed state blocks writes; releasing the older success rejects as superseded and cannot restore readiness. A new successful explicit check restores readiness and permits exactly one deliberate write. Existing compatibility tests additionally cover a newer semantically incompatible response, unavailable/legacy discovery, captured requirements and additive extensions.

gates.fullMeasuredQuality: blocked: npm test clears coverage; no browser coverage exists for merge-coverage.ts. This is not a quality pass.

execution.findings: No runtime conformance defect found in the six selected criteria. Added explicit criterion-level cross-interface regression coverage rather than speculative refactoring.

limits: SQLite local process/loopback interfaces only; no authenticated hosting, organizational permissions, other adapter or representative-human validation.
No new browser run, latency/throughput benchmark, deployment or arbitrary-scale readiness claim. These criteria require no UI interaction.
Compatibility tests deliberately intercept responses to exercise incompatible server versions and malformed messages; no alternate server implementation is claimed.
Null command lookup means no visible committed success, not proof an in-flight command failed. Tests recover a known committed result; clients never automatically replay.
A complete recorded export proves native/history/evidence preservation in the disposable scenarios; the command ledger is checked separately because it is not exported.
Source hashes and native evidence do not retain external source bytes. The report is a version-controlled exact-result artifact; no standards-conformance claim.
